name: Workshop - Brightwave (Campaign Replication & Budget Rescue)
narrative:
Priya Anand, a non-technical CMO of a $1B consumer brand, opens the marketing console and sees what her team has felt for three weeks: a cluster of campaigns glowing two colors — green winners quietly outperforming on a specific channel-and-creative combination, and red underperformers burning roughly a fifth of the paid budget while the quarter is still in play. Attribution used to land weeks later, too late to act.

Priya asks about the worst campaign: CMP-0000214, a ROAS of 1.1 against a portfolio of winners near 4.0 — how does she replicate what's working across the ones that aren't? The assistant isolates the drivers of the top campaigns (channel mix, creative, targeting) and ranks the three plays for the underperformer (apply the winning campaign's template, reallocate its budget to a proven winner, or pause it), each with the projected ROAS lift and the spend at stake, from a heuristic scored on Brightwave's own campaign history. It recommends replicating the winner, drafts the new campaign brief, and stops for approval. Priya approves; the action writes back to Lakebase with an audit trail — governed campaign and spend data turned into a mid-quarter marketing move, on-brand, with the assistant's content-generation AI spend capped and observable.

Workshop training template (Tech Summit FY27 Live Days): data generator + full spec set (SDP pipeline, metric views, ROAS-lift model, dashboard + Genie, and a Databricks App with a Visualize/Assist/Act agent loop over Lakebase). Maps to the three build milestones — Lakebase, Databricks Apps, Unity AI Gateway.
